title: Immunome Presents Additional Clinical Data for Varegacestat in Desmoid Tumors at ESMO 2026
summary: BOTHELL, Wash. – Immunome, Inc. (Nasdaq: IMNM), a clinical-stage targeted oncology company committed to developing first-in-class and best-in-class targeted cancer therapies…
body_markdown:
BOTHELL, Wash. –


[Immunome, Inc.](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fimmunome.com%2F&esheet=54628040&newsitemid=20261026171397&lan=en-US&anchor=Immunome%2C+Inc.&index=1&md5=9053bfe868582f64b6f2a3a4e096201f) (Nasdaq: IMNM), a clinical-stage targeted oncology company committed to developing first-in-class and best-in-class targeted cancer therapies, today announced the presentation of additional clinical data for varegacestat, its investigational, oral, once-daily gamma secretase inhibitor, at the 2026 European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress. The data were featured in four presentations, including a rapid oral presentation on patient-reported outcomes from the Phase 3 RINGSIDE trial in patients with progressing desmoid tumors and three posters providing further analyses of varegacestat’s clinical profile.


“For patients with desmoid tumors, treatment goals extend beyond tumor shrinkage to include symptom relief and improved physical function,” said Bob Lechleider, M.D., Chief Medical Officer of Immunome. “These presentations build on the previously reported RINGSIDE results and offer additional insight into varegacestat’s potential to address the burden of this disease.”


The rapid oral presentation included exploratory analyses of patient-reported symptom burden and physical function that complement the pain results previously presented at ASCO 2026. At week 48, patients treated with varegacestat had a least-squares mean change from baseline in the GODDESS TSS-5 symptom score of -1.50 vs. +0.59 for patients receiving placebo, with lower scores indicating lower symptom burden. On the PROMIS Physical Function measure, where higher scores indicate better function, the least-squares mean change from baseline was +3.90 with varegacestat vs. -3.04 with placebo at week 48.


Immunome also presented three posters covering RINGSIDE primary efficacy results and T2-weighted MRI signal intensity changes, a detailed analysis of safety in RINGSIDE, and exposure-response relationships across the varegacestat clinical development program.


As previously reported and presented at the 2026 ASCO Annual Meeting, RINGSIDE met its primary endpoint and all key secondary endpoints. The confirmed objective response rate (ORR) based on RECIST v1.1 was 56% with varegacestat vs. 9% with placebo (p<0.0001), as assessed by blinded independent central review. Varegacestat improved progression-free survival (PFS) vs. placebo, with an 84% reduction in the risk of disease progression or death (hazard ratio \[HR\] = 0.16, 95% confidence interval \[CI\]: 0.071, 0.375; p<0.0001). The trial also demonstrated statistically significant improvements in change in tumor volume at week 24 and change in worst pain intensity score at week 12 (p<0.0001 for each), with a clinically meaningful pain difference evident by week 4. The most common adverse events with varegacestat were diarrhea, fatigue, rash, nausea, and cough.


**ESMO 2026 Presentation Details**


All four presentations took place on October 26, 2026, in Madrid.


**Rapid Oral Presentation**


3724RO – Patient Reported Outcomes (PROs) with Varegacestat Versus Placebo (PBO) in Progressing Desmoid Tumors: Results from RINGSIDE Part B


Presenter: Dr. Winette T. van der Graaf


**Poster Presentations**


3754P – Detailed Safety Analysis of Varegacestat Treatment for Desmoid Tumors in the RINGSIDE Phase 3 Trial


Presenter: Dr. Piotr Rutkowski


3755P – RINGSIDE Phase 3 Study of Varegacestat in Desmoid Tumors: Primary Results and T2-weighted Signal Intensity Changes


Presenter: Dr. Bernd Kasper


3777P – Exposure-Response (ER) Analyses to Support the Recommended Dose of Varegacestat (VAR) for Patients (Pts) With Desmoid Tumors (DT)

**About the RINGSIDE Trial**


The global, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 RINGSIDE trial (ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04871282) evaluated the efficacy and safety of varegacestat in patients with progressing desmoid tumors. A total of 156 patients were randomized to receive varegacestat 1.2 mg daily or placebo until disease progression or death, representing the largest randomized study in this population. The primary endpoint of the trial was progression-free survival as assessed by blinded independent central review. Statistically controlled secondary endpoints were confirmed ORR using RECIST v1.1 and change in tumor volume at week 24, both determined by blinded independent central review, as well as change in pain intensity at week 12 as determined using a patient-reported outcome instrument. Additional secondary endpoints included duration of response, best reduction in tumor volume, patient-reported outcomes, and safety and tolerability. RINGSIDE includes an open-label extension phase, which is ongoing.


**About Desmoid Tumors**


Desmoid tumors (also known as aggressive fibromatosis or desmoid-type fibromatosis) are aggressive non-metastatic soft tissue tumors that are prone to recurrence. Approximately 1,000-1,650 people are diagnosed with desmoid tumors each year in the United States, and there are approximately 10,000-11,000 actively managed patients. Those affected face debilitating pain, deformity, and, in some cases, life-threatening organ damage. The chronic pain and physical limitations associated with desmoid tumors lead to a high clinical burden and impaired quality of life. Although desmoid tumors are not considered cancerous, they often require systemic treatment to prevent permanent disability and alleviate disease burden.


**About Varegacestat**


Varegacestat is an investigational, oral, once-daily gamma secretase inhibitor. In December 2025, Immunome reported positive topline results for the Phase 3 RINGSIDE trial of varegacestat in adults with progressing desmoid tumors. Immunome’s NDA for varegacestat was accepted by the FDA in July 2026 (PDUFA target action date of April 28, 2027) and the company plans to submit a Marketing Authorization Application to the European Medicines Agency for varegacestat by the end of 2026.


**About Immunome, Inc.**


Immunome is a clinical-stage targeted oncology company committed to developing first-in-class and best-in-class targeted cancer therapies. We are advancing an innovative portfolio of therapeutics, supported by a leadership team with deep experience in the design, development, and commercialization of cutting-edge therapies, including antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs). Our pipeline includes varegacestat, an investigational, oral, once-daily gamma secretase inhibitor for which an NDA has been accepted by the U.S. FDA; IM-1021, a clinical-stage ROR1 ADC; IM-1617, a clinical-stage solid tumor ADC; IM-3050, a clinical-stage FAP-targeted radiotherapy; and IM-1340, an IND-cleared solid tumor ADC.
